subject: Harmonize renewal: mid-contract uplift + co-term holdback options
messages:
From: Nadia Collins <procurement@alcyon.ai>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 19 Jul 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal planning — uplift + co-term holdback ideas

Hi Tessa / Ben,

Hope you both are well. Our renewal is coming up in Q4 and we've had a faster-than-forecasted adoption of a few new LLM features; forecast now points to ~40% growth vs. current commit through Dec. Before we sign anything, procurement and finance asked me to surface two things we want to explore with Redwood: 

1) Mid-contract uplift: we expect to need an incremental capacity top-up starting in September. We'd like to understand fair pricing for a temporary mid-term uplift that doesn't lock us into an immediate annual re-commitment.
2) Co-term + holdback: if we co-term now to sync to our fiscal year (Jan 1), finance prefers a small holdback credit or smoothing so the yearly budget impact is manageable.

To move forward we need: a short summary of options (commercial), a draft amendment we can circulate, and a sample invoicing cadence (pro-rate + holdback mechanics). I've attached our usage snapshot for July so you can see the ramp.

Can we set a 30-min call this week to run through options? Prefer Tue/Wed morning PT.

Thanks,
Nadia Collins
Director, Procurement
Alcyon AI

Attachments: usage-snapshot-Jul2027.csv (CSV, 120KB)

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Nadia Collins <procurement@alcyon.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Jul 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal planning — uplift + co-term holdback ideas

Hi Nadia — thanks for the context and the snapshot, that ramp is clear. High level we can offer three practical paths; I'll summarize quickly and then propose next steps: 

Option A — Staged Top-up (no annualize): short-term uplift (3-6 months) priced at a marginal uplift rate (typically 12–18% over hosted unit price). Invoiced pro-rata monthly. No co-term change.

Option B — Co-term + Holdback (recommended if you want budget smoothing): move your contract to Jan 1 co-term, add the mid-contract uplift as a temporary bucket, and apply a 15% holdback credit on the uplift amount to be reconciled at next renewal based on realized consumption. This reduces near-term invoice impact while preserving committed capacity economics.

Option C — Annualize now with staged discount: annualize the uplift into the commit for the remainder of the contract but apply a stepped discount schedule (higher discount in year 1, normalizing in year 2) to reflect the short runway.

Next steps I propose:
- Short call (30m) to pick the best commercial path — Tue 21 Jul 9:30 or Wed 22 Jul 10:00 PT?
- If you like Option B, I can circulate a one-page amendment draft and a sample invoice schedule with holdback mechanics.

I've attached a brief playbook we use internally that shows math examples for each path. Happy to walk through on the call.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Phone: (415) 555-0182

Attachment: Redwood_Amendment_draft_v1.pdf (PDF, stub)

Thanks Nadia / Tessa — quick technical note from a capacity and SLA perspective to support Option B (co-term + holdback). 

- Capacity buffer: We recommend a 20% burst buffer on the uplift bucket for the first 60 days to avoid cold-start latency while KV-caches warm. This is billable only if consumed; it's a protective runway.
- Autoscaling policy: If you anticipate spiky inference (e.g., batch re-indexing windows), we can set a burst cap and automatic fallback to a slightly lower-cost variant. That config will appear on the amendment as an optional line item.
- Measurement: We'll use token consumption + peak RPS windows from your usage snapshot to generate a sample SLA-friendly invoice schedule.

I'll attach a short capacity worksheet; if you'd like, I can run a quick simulation during the call and show expected monthly spend under Option B vs A/C. 

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachment: capacity-plan.xlsx (XLSX, stub)
